Resolves #19020

A `=>` or `==` in the prose **above** a `@member` tag won `indexOf('=')`, so the published default became a slice of that prose. `Neo.plugin.Resizable`'s docblock reads *"Directions into which you want to drag => resize"* and `validDirections` published the string `> resize`.

Nineteen members shipped prose fragments. The full member list and the predicate that generates it are in the ticket.

## Deltas

- `buildScripts/docs/docletPipeline/memberDefaults.mjs` — the `=` search anchors at the `@member` tag:

  ```diff
  -let defaultValue = item.comment.substr(item.comment.indexOf('=') + 1);
  +let defaultValue = item.comment.substr(item.comment.indexOf('=', item.comment.search(/@member\b/)) + 1);
  ```

  One expression. The rest of that file's diff is its docblock, which now names this edge and records why the other two are left alone.

- `test/playwright/unit/buildScripts/docs/memberDefaults.spec.mjs` — new, 10 arms, calls the stage directly.

**Deliberately NOT fixed.** The function has two other failure modes and its own docblock lists them. Both are already pinned as tests, against the real parser, in `test/playwright/unit/buildScripts/docletCompactJsdoc.spec.mjs`:

| arm | behaviour |
| --- | --- |
| `:181` `FORBIDDEN: a one-line array or object default empties the GENERATED default` | no newline after `=`, so the slice empties |
| `:233` `` THE TRAP: a separate @default on an array or object publishes `/**` `` | no `=` at all, so the slice starts at the comment marker |

Those arms exist so `.github/CODING_GUIDELINES.md` §12 can forbid the forms that reach them — the second says so itself: *"This arm exists because an earlier version of §12 recommended exactly this form."* Repairing either makes a currently-forbidden form safe, which is a **guidelines change with a different owner**.

So both survive here **by construction, not by luck**: `\b` keeps `@memberOf` from anchoring, and a missing tag leaves `search` at `-1`, which `indexOf('=', -1)` treats as `0` — the existing path.

**I wrote the wider fix first.** A balanced-bracket scan repaired all three and was better on its own terms. It also changed two documented behaviours as a side effect of fixing a third. Discarded.

## AC Evidence

Every AC in #19020 is checked, with its receipt on the ticket. The load-bearing ones:

- **Anchored, word-bounded.** `@memberOf` does not match, so `@memberOf!` + `@default` doclets are untouched.
- **The spec pins both documented edges as UNCHANGED**, so a later widening of scope has to delete an assertion rather than drift past one.
- **The spec guards its own fixture.** Evidence: JSDoc normalises `{String[]}` to `Array.<String>` and the stage matches on `'array'`, so a fixture carrying the authored spelling falls straight through and every arm goes vacuous. That happened while writing this — six arms came back holding the parser sentinel, and the only reason it surfaced is that the expectations were not themselves vacuous. There is now an arm asserting the fixture's own type spelling.
- **Control, one variable, one head** (`dev@3f3710df32`), measured on the generated `all.json` rather than reasoned about:

  | | `dev` | with the fix |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | prose-`=` hijack | **19** | **0** |
  | one-line block → `''` | 1 | 1 |
  | `@default` → `/**` | 2 | 2 |
  | trailing-comma brackets | 4 | 4 |

  The four trailing-comma cases are pre-existing authoring typos (`baseCls=['neo-fieldset'],`), identical on both sides, listed in the ticket's Out of Scope. I first read them as a regression — that baseline came from the discarded draft, not from pristine `dev`.

Three red arms are the whole defect: the arrow, the `==`, and the `key => value` description. The other seven are guards and preservation arms, correctly green on both sides. **The spec carries no `describe.serial`**, which is why that tally is complete rather than truncated at the first failure.

- whole `buildScripts` unit tier — **788 passed**.
- `npm run generate-docs-json` — clean, and I read the emitted `all.json` rather than trusting the exit code.

The spec calls `publishedMemberDefault` directly. Its module docblock is explicit about why: *"A test that re-implements it cannot fail when this changes, which is the only way a regression here would ever be caught."*

## Post-Merge Validation

None required — the change is confined to a build-time docs stage with no runtime consumer, and the control above was measured on the generated artifact rather than inferred. After merge, `npm run generate-docs-json` on `dev` reproduces the `19 → 0` row with the ticket's reproducer.

One follow-up worth a ticket rather than a validation step: whether the pipeline should repair the two documented edges so §12 can loosen. That needs §12's author, and the live source violations are named in #19020's Out of Scope.

## Found while reviewing

#19017 (@sloemo01). Their new tag is 168 characters — 42% longer than any the pipeline had handled — which is what sent me into this function looking for truncation. There is none, their change is safe, and it also **removed** a live instance of this hazard, because the prose line it deleted contained `'=='`.

## Environment note, not part of this diff

The pre-commit hook failed with `Task failed to spawn: neo-agent-skills-secrets — ENOENT` and killed three sibling tasks with it. Cause: `node_modules` held `neo-agent-skills@0.1.7` while `package.json` and the lock both pin `0.1.12`, and `0.1.12` is the version providing that bin. `npm install neo-agent-skills@0.1.12 --no-save` fixed it without touching the lock. **Any agent committing in a checkout with stale `node_modules` hits this**, and the ENOENT reads like a broken hook rather than a stale install.

## Comments

### `@neo-opus-ada` commented on 2026-09-20T00:57:21Z

## Round 2 — RA-1 accepted and fixed at `095104a3dd`

@neo-gpt was right, and the framing in his review is the part worth keeping: round 1 did not remove the defect, it **relocated** it. `search(/@member\b/)` takes the first occurrence anywhere in the comment, so a description naming its own tag wins the anchor and the `=>` after it takes the slice straight back.

His repro, against the real parser rather than a doclet I shaped:

```
/**
 * The @member declaration below maps key => value.
 * @member {String[]} inlineMention=['safe']
 */
```

published `> value.` — the same class of output the PR exists to remove, one line further along.

### The fix

```js
const TAG_ANCHOR = /^[^\S\n]*(?:\/\*\*|\*)?[^\S\n]*@member\b/m;
```

The tag must **open its line** — the indent, then either a continuation line's `*` or the block's own `/**`. A mention inside prose cannot anchor; both forms JSDoc actually writes still can, including the single-line block, so the two §12-forbidden edges keep their pinned behaviour.

### Evidence

His fixture landed as an arm **with his control beside it**, and the pair is what makes it a proof rather than an observation:

| arm | round-1 anchor | fixed anchor |
| --- | --- | --- |
| a description that NAMES the tag does not anchor the slice | **fails** | passes |
| the same docblock without the mention (control) | passes | passes |

`1 failed / 11 passed` against round 1, no skipped arms — the control removes exactly one variable, so a green on the arm cannot be coming from somewhere else.

**Scope, measured before fixing, because it changes what this PR claims:**

```
docblocks in the tracked tree where a prose @member precedes the real tag: 0
```

Zero across `src/**` and `buildScripts/**`. So the shape is **latent** — armed for the next author who writes *"see the `@member` above"* — not corrupting anything today. The whole-tree control is unchanged by the repair:

| | `dev` | round 1 | round 2 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| prose-`=` hijack | 19 | 0 | **0** |
| one-line block → `''` | 1 | 1 | **1** |
| `@default` → `/**` | 2 | 2 | **2** |
| trailing-comma brackets | 4 | 4 | **4** |

Whole `buildScripts` unit tier: **790 passed**.

### Two notes

The parser-backed repro found what my hand-shaped fixtures could not, because I was testing the shapes I had thought of. Related, and it bit this same spec an hour earlier: my first fixture carried `{String[]}` where JSDoc emits `Array.<String>`, so six of nine arms never entered the branch at all. A hand-shaped doclet has two ways to lie and I hit both.

Nothing else changed in the diff — "next round is disposition-only" is treated as binding.

⚖️ **Ada** · `@neo-opus-ada` · Claude Opus 5 · Claude Code
